subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: all patients met Berlin ARDS with PaO2/FiO2 < 150. mixed_bmi: median BMI 28.1 kg/m2 but the study explicitly analyses obese (n=9, BMI >= 30) and non-obese (n=11) subgroups. timing_subgroup: median time from ARDS diagnosis to inclusion 39 (27–51) hours, i.e. under 48 h at the median, within the 72-h window; classified early_within_48h although the IQR crosses 48 h. ptp_target_subgroups: the study applies both an absolute end-expiratory PL target (0-10 cmH2O, Talmor table) and an elastance-derived end-inspiratory PL target (20-22 cmH2O).

reported_subgroups.outcome_name: PEEP levels determined by the two titration strategies (PEEPPL, insp vs PEEPPL, exp)
reported_subgroups.result_verbatim: PEEPPL, insp was higher than PEEPPL, exp in the non-obese patients (n = 11; 16 (14-18.5) cmH2O and 10 (7.5–15) cmH2O, respectively; p = 0.03). But no difference was observed between PEEPPL, insp and PEEPPL, exp in the obese patients (n = 9; 16 (12–18) cmH2O and 15 (15–18) cmH2O, respectively; p = 0.78)

provenance.quote: PEEPPL, insp was higher than PEEPPL, exp in the non-obese patients (n = 11; 16 (14-18.5) cmH2O and 10 (7.5–15) cmH2O, respectively; p = 0.03). But no difference was observed between PEEPPL, insp and PEEPPL, exp in the obese patients (n = 9; 16 (12–18) cmH2O and 15 (15–18) cmH2O, respectively; p = 0.78) (Fig. 2A).

reported_subgroups.outcome_name: CRS, BMI, Pplat, respiratory system driving pressure and transpulmonary driving pressure at PEEP 5 cmH2O
reported_subgroups.result_verbatim: Compared to the patients with PEEPPL, exp lower than PEEPPL, insp, those with PEEPPL, exp higher than or equal to PEEPPL, insp were characterized by significantly lower CRS and higher BMI, Pplat, respiratory system driving pressure and transpulmonary driving pressure at PEEP 5 cmH2O.

provenance.quote: Compared to the patients with PEEPPL, exp lower than PEEPPL, insp, those with PEEPPL, exp higher than or equal to PEEPPL, insp were characterized by signifi­ cantly lower CRS and higher BMI, Pplat, respiratory system driving pressure and transpulmonary driving pressure at PEEP 5 cmH2O.
provenance.location: Results, PEEP levels determined by the two transpulmonary pressure-based titration strategies, p. 4

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: COHORTS.md suspects an 'angers' cluster with pavlovsky_2024 (same ICU, shared authorship: Pavlovsky, Desprez, Richard, Chean, Mercat, Beloncle appear on both). Checks run on this report: (1) registration — this study is NCT03281473, registered 12 September 2017; pavlovsky_2024 (ref 23, Ann Intensive Care 2024, EIT/recruitment-to-inflation ratio physiologic study) is a different protocol and its registration is not stated in this PDF; (2) enrolment window — this study enrolled October 2018 to January 2022; (3) design and population — this is a randomized crossover of two PL-based PEEP titration strategies in 20 patients, whereas pavlovsky_2024 compares EIT-based and respiratory-mechanics-based PEEP methods, a distinct protocol. Pavlovsky 2024 additionally stated that 10 of its COVID-ARDS patients were published earlier in a paper not in this folder. I could not conclusively confirm or refute patient sharing from this report alone; cohort_id left null pending adjudication.
unclear_items: extraction_flags.cohort_id — possible 'angers' cluster with pavlovsky_2024 on shared ICU/authors; registration and protocol differ but patient-level overlap cannot be excluded from this report alone.

extraction_flags.general_notes: Additional paired results reported in text but not in Table 2: PEEPPL, insp and PEEPPL, exp were higher than the Express-strategy PEEP in 7 (35%) and 6 (30%) patients; the difference between PEEPPL, insp and PEEPPL, exp was at least 3 cmH2O in 14 (70%) patients; PEEPPL, exp was lower than PEEPPL, insp in 12 patients (60%) and higher than or equal in 8 (40%); PL, exp was negative in 2 (10%) patients with the PL, insp strategy and calculated PL, insp was higher than 22 cmH2O in 7 (35%) patients with the PL, exp strategy; carry-over test on PaO2/FiO2 using a linear mixed-effects model p = 0.07. Tidal volume was 400 (362–450) mL and unchanged across conditions. Obese/non-obese and COVID/non-COVID subgroup data are in additional file 1 (Tables S3-S6), not provided. The proportion of patients with Pplat > 30 cmH2O or driving pressure > 14 cmH2O did not differ between strategies (additional file 1, Table S6).
